newsitem.title: FRANCE: Breakdown of French oil disruption at 1200 GMT.
newsitem.headline: Breakdown of French oil disruption at 1200 GMT.

text.p: A one-day French oil industry strike over job cuts on Tuesday disrupted at least three oil refineries and halted core distillation at a fourth, but did not produce a nationwide shutdown, unions and oil firms said.
Several plants were however considering action for later in the day, bringing the number of refineries which might be hit by the end of Tuesday to around half of France's total.
Five unions had called a nationwide oil industry strike over plans to cut an estimated 1,500 jobs in the refining sector.

Union officials have since said that only major plants, especially in the southeast, were likely to be hit and three Elf refineries have been excluded from the action after workers there ended a nine-day strike last Friday.
Following is a list of Tuesday's action that could be confirmed by both sides as of 1200 GMT.
Refinery capacity is in barrels per day.
Except where stated, all action refers to 24-hour strikes or deliberate slowdowns which began on Tuesday.
BP Lavera 200,000 Slowed to minimum rate
Cie Rhenane (CRR) Reichstett 80,000 No action reported
(note: Elf plants near normal after strike ended on Friday).
Shell Berre 128,000 Strike began on Monday,
